summary.headline: Hindalco Q2 FY27: consolidated EBITDA up 52% YoY to INR13,869 crore; India copper record INR1,673 crore, with INR350-400 crore called non-recurring.
summary.overview: Consolidated EBITDA rose 52% YoY to INR13,869 crore and consolidated PAT rose 59% to INR7,533 crore, with India business EBITDA up 66% to INR9,011 crore. India aluminium upstream EBITDA was INR7,009 crore (up 55%, $2,125/t), while copper posted a record INR1,673 crore that management says includes roughly INR350-400 crore of non-repeatable gains. Management guided copper to an underlying INR1,200-1,300 crore a quarter and flagged aluminium cost up about 5% QoQ on coal, with no relief until Q4. Novelis is recovering from the Oswego fire and Yeongju strike, with tariff headwinds expected to fade by Q4 and deleveraging targeted to start by FY27 end.

segments.name: India aluminium upstream
segments.commentary: Shipments up 1% YoY, revenue up 33% YoY, EBITDA INR7,009 crore ($2,125/t). Higher net export premium (to non-MJP countries) and value-added products such as conductor cables supported margins despite a ~5% QoQ cost increase.

segments.name: India aluminium downstream
segments.commentary: Shipments 119 KT (+6% YoY), EBITDA INR329 crore (+26% YoY), $289/t. Management expects EBITDA/t to cross $300 as Aditya FRP (now at 50% loading) qualifies battery foil, ULG foil and can body stock.

segments.name: India copper
segments.commentary: Record EBITDA INR1,673 crore (+164% YoY) on 116 KT metal shipments and 96 KT CCR. Includes ~INR350-400 crore of non-sustainable items (slag sales, derivative noise, precious metal sales). Underlying run rate guided at INR1,200-1,300 crore a quarter.

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Oswego hot mill back to normal production; cumulative insurance recoveries $519 million through September. Yeongju strike cost ~$20 million in Q2, similar impact expected in Q3; a further $47 million of insurance recoveries expected in EBITDA by FY27 end. Bay Minette's first cold-rolled coil was produced in September 2026, with commercial shipments from Q1 FY28. Long-term EBITDA/t guidance of $600 unchanged.

guidance_outlook: Aluminium cost of production expected up ~5% QoQ in Q3 on coal; Q4 costs to decline as coal supply improves.
Copper underlying quarterly EBITDA guided at INR1,200-1,300 crore, driven by sulfuric acid (about INR14,000-15,000/t expected in Q3-Q4) and precious metals.
Novelis tariff headwinds expected to become marginal by Q4 FY27; Q3 Yeongju impact ~$20 million; shipments expected to pick up from Q4.
Novelis consolidated net debt/EBITDA to reach about 4x in Q4 FY27, then 2.5x-2.8x over the next two years; return to positive free cash flow targeted by FY27 end.
FY27 capex about INR12,000-13,000 crore; FY28 substantially higher, with FY28-29 outflow described as quite high; consolidated net debt/EBITDA to be kept around 2x.
Chakla coal mine expected to deliver coal by mid-FY28; Bandha coal expected in H2 FY28. Alumina index expected near $400/t in FY28 from ~$350/t currently.
capex_capacity: Commissioning: Pakhajan copper recycling plant in December 2026; Aditya Alumina Refinery and first 180 KT Aditya smelter line in December 2027; second Aditya smelter line and copper smelter in December 2028.

Next growth project after these to be Mahan smelter expansion (370 KT), currently in EC approval and licensing; further copper recycling expansion from 50 KT to 150 KT. Management says one new project roughly every 1.5 years.

Over INR50,000 crore of expansions under execution in India, with another INR50,000 crore under evaluation; over INR1 lakh crore of growth investment over five years. About INR20,000 crore of the first INR50,000 crore expected to be spent by FY27 end.
Novelis FY28 capex expected to normalise to about $500-600 million (maintenance plus projects).
Upstream optionality: Mahan can add 360 KT (and up to 720 KT more); Aditya has no further land after the 360 KT expansion. Downstream: Aditya cold mill of 170 KT could be added to 600 KT.
Renewables at 643 MW at end-Q2 plus 35 MW pumped-storage tie-ups; target 884 MW by FY27 exit, plus 125 MW RE-RTC capacity.
demand_pricing: Global aluminium deficit expected at ~0.8 Mt in CY2026 (earlier view ~1 Mt); roughly 0.5 Mt deficit in the quarter. Global production ~19 Mt (-1% YoY); consumption ~19 Mt (+1% YoY).
India aluminium demand ~1.7 Mt in Q2 FY27 (+6% YoY), led by automotive. Management sees Indian demand CAGR of ~7%.
Refined copper demand in India 388 KT (-3% YoY). Copper concentrate TC/RC spot at -48 to -58 c/lb; management says long-term contracts secure concentrate supply.
Premium (MJP) was ~$270 in Q3 per management and expected in $200-250 range in Q4; Q3 MJP already down by more than $100. Q2 benefited from exports to high-premium non-MJP countries.
Hedging: about 29% of H2 FY27 aluminium at $3,000/t and 21% of currency at INR93/$; about 26% of FY28 hedged at $3,168/t.
LME outlook for next year cited at $2,600-2,800/t; management uses $2,600/t for smelter IRR assumptions and targets mid-teens IRR at that price.
Cash cost highest-end of aluminium curve ~ $2,000-2,200/t. Coal is ~40% of the cost curve impact; CP coke also rising but not expected to rise much further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off in copper EBITDA and what is the sustainable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR350-400 crore is non-repeatable (slag sales accruals, derivative noise, extra precious metal sales); underlying run rate INR1,200-1,300 crore a quarter, driven by sulfuric acid at ~INR16,000/t now versus ~INR7,000/t a year earlier, with about 300 KT of acid a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did aluminium EBITDA hold up despite lower LME and higher costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher net premium from exports to non-MJP countries and better pricing on value-added products such as conductor cables lifted EBITDA/t, despite ~5% cost increase QoQ on coal.

qa_highlights.question: How will Novelis earnings predictability look for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited tariffs fading by Q4, a $20 million Yeongju impact in Q3 and then none, $47 million more insurance recoveries by FY27 end, and shipments recovering from Q4 as customer supply chains normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the pot relining capitalisation impacting EBITDA and depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: about INR130 crore added to EBITDA and INR130 crore to depreciation per quarter going forward, with Q2 including some catch-up for Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are alumina sales and the Q3 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: External alumina sales were 194 KT in Q2 and are expected at 190-200 KT in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is India's net cash position and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: India treasury about INR16,000 crore, net cash about INR9,000 crore after long-term loans of INR6,000-7,000 crore; India net debt/EBITDA -0.35x. India H1 capex about INR6,000 crore; FY27 expected INR12,000-13,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the drivers and IRRs behind new smelter investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets mid-teens IRR at $2,600/t aluminium, with constraints on execution capability and balance sheet rather than utilisation; Indian demand growth of ~7% CAGR is assumed.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA up 55% YoY; revenue up 33% YoY; shipments up 1% YoY
EBITDA up 26% YoY (from INR261 crore); shipments up 6% YoY

financial_highlights.value: INR1,673 crore (record); metal shipments 116 KT; CCR 96 KT
financial_highlights.change: up 164% YoY; metal shipments up 2% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Non-LME-linked businesses EBITDA (Novelis, aluminium downstream, copper)

risks_watch: Copper: track whether the ~INR1,200-1,300 crore underlying quarterly EBITDA holds as sulfuric acid (~INR16,000/t now, guided INR14,000-15,000/t for Q3-Q4) normalises; ~50% of copper EBITDA is non-copper by-products.
Aluminium: coal-driven cost up ~5% QoQ expected again in Q3; relief only in Q4 and depends on Chakla (mid-FY28) and Bandha (H2 FY28) mines; CP coke still rising; MJP already down >$100 in Q3.
Novelis: tariff headwinds to fade by Q4, Yeongju impact ~$20 million in Q3, $47 million insurance recoveries by FY27 end, shipments recovery from Q4; net debt/EBITDA ~4x in Q4 FY27.

Capex and leverage: FY27 capex INR12,000-13,000 crore, FY28 to be 'substantially higher' with figure due at February results; consolidated net debt/EBITDA kept around 2x; management declined to confirm peak net debt timing.
Project execution: EPC capacity constraints and balance sheet gate the next projects (Mahan 370 KT, EC approval pending); one new project roughly every 1.5 years.
Pot relining capitalisation adds ~INR130 crore to EBITDA and ~INR130 crore to depreciation per quarter going forward, which flatters EBITDA optics versus underlying.
key_quotes: Copper is expected to deliver an underlying quarterly EBITDA of around INR1,200 crores on a normalized basis, underscoring the strength and resilience of this business.
There were a couple of things that happened. We had a certain amount of copper slag sales where our accruals and what we realized by selling was higher.
Next year, it will go back to normal maintenance plus project around $500 million -$600 million levels.
It is actually an execution capability and the balance sheet. Because we are working with one large EPC contractor as our partner.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the India aluminium and copper operations and on the Novelis recovery timeline, quantifying most swing factors (tariffs, Yeongju, insurance, copper one-offs). It was more cautious and less specific on the timing of the INR50,000 crore project pipeline, on FY28 capex and debt, and on coal normalisation, deferring several numbers to the February results.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Aluminium EBITDA $2,125/t in Q2 is supported by export premium, but coal costs rise ~5% QoQ in Q3 with relief only in Q4, and downstream EBITDA/t is guided to cross $300 (currently $289/t) as Aditya FRP reaches 50% loading; copper underlying falls to INR1,200-1,300 crore.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pakhajan copper recycling plant commissioning Dec 2026 (Q3 FY27), Aditya Alumina Refinery and first 180 KT Aditya smelter line Dec 2027 (Q1 FY28 window is near; firmly dated), with Renewables rising from 643 MW to 884 MW by FY27 exit, though the big smelter line falls outside the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Novelis shipments expected to pick up from Q4 as Oswego hot mill is back to normal; India aluminium demand ~1.7 Mt (+6% YoY) with ~7% CAGR, though India upstream shipments grew only 1% YoY in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR12,000-13,000 crore with FY28 'substantially higher' and about INR20,000 crore of the first INR50,000 crore expected to be spent by FY27 end; Mahan 370 KT expansion is next in line but still in EC approval, so a formal new-project announcement is likely but timing depends on approvals and EPC capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Premium (MJP) already down more than $100 in Q3 to about $270 and expected $200-250 in Q4, and LME outlook $2,600-2,800/t is below current levels, which limits upside to guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Aluminium cost guided up ~5% QoQ in Q3 on coal, Yeongju strike costs ~$20 million in Q3, and copper underlying is INR1,200-1,300 crore against a record INR1,673 crore including INR350-400 crore one-offs, so the reported run-rate will step down.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aditya FRP at 50% loading is expected to qualify battery foil, ULG foil and can body stock, and Novelis Bay Minette produced first cold-rolled coil in Sep 2026 with commercial shipments from Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Novelis deleveraging to about 4x in Q4 FY27 then 2.5x-2.8x
rows.why: Management guided Novelis net debt/EBITDA to about 4x in Q4 FY27 and then 2.5x-2.8x over two years, with positive FCF targeted by FY27 end; $47 million more insurance recoveries expected by FY27 end.

rows.label: Coal supply relief via Chakla and Bandha mines
rows.why: Chakla coal expected by mid-FY28 and Bandha in H2 FY28; aluminium cost relief depends on these, with alumina index expected near $400/t in FY28 from about $350/t now.

rows.label: Net export premium to non-MJP countries
rows.why: Q2 benefited from exports to high-premium non-MJP countries, but MJP has fallen more than $100 in Q3, so this support is shrinking.

tone.note: Management was confident on India aluminium and copper operations and on the Novelis recovery, quantifying tariffs, Yeongju and copper one-offs, but cautious on FY28 capex, the INR50,000 crore project timing, debt peak and coal normalisation; analysts pushed on the sustainability of copper and alumi
